title: Orchestrate CI-driven lightweight onboarding + staged profile publish
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a CI-driven orchestrator that produces reproducible model artifacts, generates canonical performance profiles, signs artifacts, and publishes staged profile manifests for automated canary rollouts. This ticket covers the minimal viable flow that will let an engineer push a model branch -> CI produces build + perf run -> signature + profile manifest -> staged publish to registry -> orchestrator schedules canary cohort and publishes telemetry hooks for gating.

Motivation: Current onboarding is manual and error-prone: performance profiles are hand-recorded and promotion is manual. We need a repeatable, auditable CI path so Dedicated/Private customers can rely on pinned model behavior and Console rollouts can automate canary phases.

High-level flow: 
1) Developer opens `model-onboard/*` PR containing model recipe + sample workloads + unit tests.
2) CI job (hermetic-builder) creates a content-addressed model bundle (container or tar) and records build metadata (git sha, toolchain hash, base image).
3) CI runs perf-harness with curated microbench workloads (short timebox, sampled seq lengths). Harness emits a deterministic perf profile JSON and summary metrics.
4) CI invokes KMS-backed signer to create a timestamped artifact signature (CI key rotation policy enforced).
5) CI publishes artifact + signature + perf profile to model-registry under `staged/<candidate>` with manifest that references the artifact hash and profile hash.
6) Release-orchestrator picks up staged manifests and creates a canary release (configurable cohort size, route weight), wires telemetry from Console to the gating pipeline.
7) Gating: canary runs for N hours, telemetry evaluated against SLOs (latency median, p75, token-cost regression). If pass -> automated promotion to `pinned` channel; if fail -> automatic retraction and notification to the PR author.

Design trade-offs and constraints: 
- CI-run perf harness must be short (to keep CI costs low) and therefore may miss long-tail regressions; we rely on canary population to catch those.
- Signing in CI uses a single CI KMS key for MVP; long-term we'll move to per-team keys and hardware-backed signing (HSM).
- Perf profiles will be content-addressed; if a profile differs for the same artifact hash we record both and mark the build for manual review.
- We avoid shipping heavy integration/e2e in CI; those will remain in nightly tests to keep per-PR latency acceptable.

Deliverables:
- CI pipeline definitions (GitHub Actions / Buildkite snippets) and hermetic builder image.
- perf-harness v1 (bench driver + small corpus) and profile serializer.
- registry manifest format (manifest v1) for staged profiles.
- orchestrator job for staged publish -> canary creation.
- Console telemetry hooks and gating rules.

acceptance_criteria: CI job creates a deterministic, content-addressed model artifact and uploads to model-registry/staged/<candidate>
Perf harness produces a profile.json with stable keys and summary metrics and is uploaded alongside the artifact
Artifact is signed by CI KMS key and signature is stored in registry with a timestamp
Release-orchestrator consumes staged manifests and creates a canary release with routing configuration
Console shows canary telemetry and gating outcome; passing canary triggers promotion to pinned channel
All produced artifacts and manifests include provenance fields: git_sha, builder_image, toolchain_hash, perf_seed

Implement CI signer step using project KMS wrapper and record signature artifact -- Asha
Define registry manifest v1 and extend model-registry API to accept staged manifests -- Marco
Implement simple orchestrator consumer that creates canary releases and posts to release-api -- Noah
Add console telemetry hooks and gating evaluation rule (SLO config) -- Priya
Write e2e smoke test that runs full flow in staging and asserts promotion/rollback behavior -- QA team
notes: We will use a 30m timebox for the perf harness in CI for MVP to keep cost predictable.
Edge case: if perf profile generation times out we still publish artifact but mark as 'profile-missing' to force manual intervention.
Consider integration with ENG-41213's hermetic CD artifacts for cross-validation during promotion.
Security: signatures currently rely on shared CI service account; follow-up ticket to rotate to per-team KMS keys.
Telemetry gate thresholds will be conservative for first 2 rollouts (reduce false positives).
